title: Uncertainty, Not Concealment: A Mechanistic Reappraisal of Sycophancy in Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.10297v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) in medical retrieval-augmented generation must be able to say when a retrieved report contradicts the X-ray, so understanding whether they can detect such conflicts is important for safe deployment. The sycophancy mask hypothesis holds that these models internally detect conflicts but refuse to report them, concealing a detected contradiction. We introduce a three-part diagnostic that separates concealment from uncertainty: representation probing, activation steering, and two-way forced choice. Across four instruction-tuned VLMs on chest X-rays, we confirm behavioral suppression of contradiction and find that a linear probe separates matched from mismatched inputs, beyond what a simple CLIP model achieves. translated_title: 不确定性而非隐瞒：对视觉-语言模型谄媚行为的机制性重新审视
translated_abstract: 医学检索增强生成中的视觉-语言模型必须能够在检索到的报告与X光片相矛盾时指出这一点，因此理解这些模型能否检测此类冲突对安全部署至关重要。谄媚掩码假说认为，这些模型在内部检测到了冲突但拒绝报告，隐瞒了已察觉的矛盾。我们提出了一个由三部分组成的诊断方法来区分隐瞒与不确定性：表征探测、激活引导和双向强制选择。在四种经过指令微调的VLM对胸部X光片的实验中，我们证实了矛盾行为受到抑制，并发现线性探针能够区分匹配与不匹配的输入，其效果超越了简单的CLIP模型。对学到的冲突方向进行引导从未引发矛盾报告，强制二选一也无法恢复矛盾输出；相反，在不匹配的样本对上，模型对图像的跨模态注意力反而下降。
tldr: 本文通过表征探测、激活引导和强制选择三类机制诊断证明，视觉-语言模型在医学影像冲突检测中的谄媚行为源于模型的不确定性，而非对已检测矛盾的刻意隐瞒。
en_tdlr: Through mechanistic diagnostics including representation probing, activation steering, and forced choice, this paper shows that sycophancy in vision-language models during medical conflict detection stems from uncertainty rather than deliberate concealment of detected contradictions.
